thread.title: Micron: EPS Peak, And Peek Into 2019 ASP Expectations - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

author: Elazar Advisors, LLC
title: Micron: EPS Peak, And Peek Into 2019 ASP Expectations - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)
text:
Micron (NASDAQ: MU ) had an important tell on their last earnings conference that says a lot of different things about the company and the industry. Gross margins probably peaked and will have some trouble into the future. While competitors are cutting capex Micron is increasing capex faster than sales. That leaves more gross margin and profit risk.
What Did Micron Say About Gross Margins? Here's what Micron said about their gross margins on their last earnings call :
"Yes. So, first of all, the gross margin guidance was 57 to 60. So, of course, if we hit the higher end of that range, it would be 140 basis points down. Clearly, tariffs are impacting us, probably to the tune of 50 to 100 basis points. And as we talked about, we’re working on steps to mitigate that. That obviously takes some time. We have to do some things operationally to get ourselves in a place where it isn’t as impactful. And so, it’ll be a quarter or two probably before we start to see some benefit from the improvement there. So, that was certainly a factor on the gross margin side."
Let's break it down.
If they hit the midpoint of their gross margin guidance they will be down roughly 300 basis points from last quarter to this quarter (sequentially). They said tariffs will be about 50-100 basis points of that.
So let's midpoint the tariffs.
75 bp divided by 300 bp is about 25%.
25% of their sequential gross margin hit will be from tariffs.
That's strange because much of their earnings call revolved around tariffs, but 75% of that hit comes from something else.
What Else Is Driving Micron's Gross Margin Drop? We know it's not tariffs.
Gross margins are affected by pricing and capacity utilization.
Let's cover them both.
Micron doesn't give expectations about pricing but they are likely telling you in 75% of that 300bp drop they are expecting some chunk from pricing.
B a sed on what they said they are expecting pricing down in the teens for 2019. That's our take.
Pricing
Let's look at Micron pricing.

DRAM is their largest business. NAND we know has been seeing price drops so DRAM is most important because it's slowing.
ASPs (average selling prices) went from growing 21% quarter to quarter to 0% in the last quarter. I think, based on their guide, the next step is that DRAM prices go negative.
Again, Micron doesn't guide to DRAM prices but 75% of their gross margin guide did to some degree.
But we'll get more granular showing they are expecting DRAM prices to go negative next year. And we'll show by how much.
Get ready.
So expect pricing to start dropping. That slows revenues.
Case in point, a report out recently said Micron is showing the most aggressive pricing of the memory Big 3.
That speaks to their gross margin guide.
What's driving that desire to be more aggressive in pricing? They are driving capex faster than peers. Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) expects capex to drop. Hynix (XHSCL) just took a chop to capex. Micron expects it to grow.
Say what you want but there were enough companies talking about slowing this quarter. Let's name a few biggies: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ), Google (NASDAQ: GOOG )(NASDAQ: GOOGL ), Texas Instruments (NASDAQ: TXN ), Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ), Skyworks (NASDAQ: SWKS ), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ). I probably missed a few.
I named chip makers because if they are slowing, they and their customers are slowing, which speaks to Micron's demand.
I named hyperscalers slowing because slowing demand can have them rethink capex budgets in the future.
That may be the reason for some reshuffling of customer inventory Micron called out last call. They said:
"And, given the kind of pricing that had existed in the DRAM market, certain customers had certain inventory levels that - certain inventory strategies that they were pursuing, and those customers have decided to adjust their inventory levels. So, that’s what we refer to in our remarks. In terms of the end market demand for those customers and end market demand for DRAM applications, that continues to be solid. It’s just an inventory adjustment approach of some of our customers."
Customers changed "certain inventory strategies." Why did they change? Because they didn't need to buy ahead of price increases any more. Prices stalled. Instead of building inventory they want to exit inventory and be clean. If they are clean and don't buy now they can buy DRAM at cheaper prices based on need.
That cycles to further hit prices. Thus Micron's gross margin guide.
Capacity Utilization
While the company's revenue growth slows as pricing accelerates on the downside their capex keeps growing.
The company said on the last earnings call that their capex spend will be faster than revenue growth.
Here's what they said:
"While our annual capital spending was well below our capex model of low-30s as a percent of revenue in fiscal 2018, we do plan to increase our capex as a percent of revenue in fiscal 2019. We currently expect our fiscal 2019 capex net of partner contributions to be in the range of $10.5 billion, plus or minus 5%."
It sounds like they under-spent on capex and based on their "well below" capex spend they want to play catch up.
Capex growing faster than sales can leave capacity under utilized which can hurt margins. Less units and more fixed assets increases the fixed asset cost per unit hurting margins. That's probably some of their guide.
Even though they were below their historical capex spend goals last year they grew capex inline with sales. Capex grew 52% in the recently completed fiscal year.
If they get back to their "model of low-30s (capex) as a percent of revenue" it implies 12% revenue growth for 2019. That's much slower than last year's 52% revenue growth.
Let's walk through the numbers.
Now For Their Down Pricing Estimates You can (sort of) back into the math to figure out what they expect for 2019 pricing. That's a big feat, especially that they don't give pricing guidance.
Here's what they said on the last earnings call about giving pricing guidance:
"And with respect to pricing, of course, we do not forecast pricing..."
They don't guide to pricing. But pricing is the most important metric that drives the EPS model both up and down. That's all the earnings leverage both up and down.
What they continued to say would paint a bullish picture of pricing.
They continued:
"...but you look at our FQ4 results, our DRAM pricing was flat and 71% gross margin, record gross margin, extremely healthy industry environment we see going forward as well for DRAM. As I talked about the demand drivers are vibrant for DRAM, they are diversified and they are secular in nature. And DRAM solutions are really bringing great value to the AI-driven kind of applications where they’re really central to that trend.
Now let's parse out what Micron expects for pricing, even though they explicitly said they will (our paraphrase) "never ever in a million years ever never ever guide to pricing. Not gonna do it."
But let's do it.
They expected $10.5B in capex for this coming year. 32% of what revenue number would be "low-30s (capex) as a percent of revenues?" (10.5 divided by 33.4).
Backing into that $33.4B for revenues using their capex would imply 12% revenue growth for 2019.
So if (a big if) they got back to their stated goal of low-30s capex to revenues you can back into their revenue targets using their expected annual capex number.
Let's now take that a step further.
12% revenue growth has two drivers - ASPs and bit growth (volumes).
They gave us their bit growth expectations for 2019 ( page 7 ). They expect 20% DRAM bit growth and roughly 42% NAND bit growth for 2019.
Lets assume that DRAM makes up 70% of their revenues for next year which is what it was last quarter ( page 14 ). That gets us to Micron's expected blended bit growth for 2019 of roughly 26-27%.
26-27% volumes + what pricing = 12% revenue growth.
Solve for "what pricing."
Pricing = down about 14%-15%
Rough numbers.
If we multiply (1+vol)*(1+price)-1= 12% revenue growth we get -11 to -12% pricing. So I think it's fair their goal for pricing is anywhere from -11 to -15%.
Backing into the numbers Micron gave us, and taking a few liberties (if you will), it looks like Micron is expecting a hit to pricing.
So this guide for gross margins of down 300 basis points makes more sense. This may not be so one quarter if Micron is expecting 2019 pricing to be down as well.
And with more capex you can be in a situation of lower capacity utilization which tends to reduce margins. Lower prices also reduce margins.
That may be another part of the 75% of their 300bp sequential drop in their gross margin guide.
Peak Earnings If the above holds true, which I'm just basing on their guide and many market factors that we all see in unison, it would mean that the August 2018 quarter will be their peak EPS quarter.
Tech stocks are driven by momentum investors. For Micron, investors and the company look at business in a very sequential fashion, not year-over-year.
Semiconductor-related companies mostly focus on sequential growth rates. Those sequential growth rates sound like they'll continue to slow and start to drop.
If each quarter EPS drops vs. the previous, momentum is gone.
Cyclical stocks tend to look cheap at peaks and expensive at troughs. That's the nature of cyclical stocks.
I think it's tough to call a bottom here.
Valuation I'm not recommending to short Micron. I generally don't recommend shorting except maybe ETFs to hedge at times.
I agree Micron looks cheap and I agree this down-cycle is probably different than past ones. But I'm not a value guy, I'm a momentum ("mo") guy. I care about trends and trends are what drive stock prices.
Valuations help but trends decide which way stocks will move in most cases. That's been my training.
So I can avoid Micron for the time being.
Value also needs to usually wait for the fundamentals to bottom and move back up. So I'd rather skip the valuation talk and just put my energy into when "the fundamentals bottom and move back up."
Conclusion Micron tried not to but I think they ended up giving a lot of information on their last earnings call. Backing into gross margins and capex tells you pricing is expected to come down more meaningfully. They need demand to pick up but it's slowing. They need that demand because their capex plans are going to run faster than revenue growth, making for EPS and margin deleverage risk.
